messages:
maya: quick heads-up — I pushed an experiment branch that switches to a probabilistic admit window for thin batches. goal: reduce 429 spikes without tanking p99.

dan: can you summarize the admit rule? is it token-budget driven or batch-size driven?

maya: token-budget primarily. rule: if current queue token estimate > target * 1.1 then start sampling admits with p=0.3, else p=1.0. also factor kv-cache hit rate: if kv_hit_rate > 0.6 bias p up.

lyra: interesting. so this is a soft-reject probe (not hard 429) — how are clients seeing it? stream of 202s or small delays?

maya: soft 429s returned for rejected requests (we mark as retryable). clients see Retry-After: 50ms plus jitter. telemetry shows a lot of retries coalescing though.

ops-bot: deploy triggered: maya/probabilistic-admit -> canary group (10%)

sam: profiler-bot — can you drop the hot path for the canary window? want to see kernel switch churn and batch formation times.

profiler-bot: attached perf snapshot: kernel_switch_count: 620 (canary) vs 1900 (baseline); avg_batch_assembly_ms: 8.2 (canary) vs 5.9 (baseline); kv_hit_rate: 0.52; token_budget_avg: 74 -> 58 after admit sampling.

dan: avg_batch_assembly rising worries me. are we creating more partial batches because admits are probabilistic?

maya: yes — admit sampling lowers queue density which slightly increases mean assembly latency for batches that do form. but overall token throughput improved and 95th latency dropped for evicted requests.

lyra: any kernel selection regressions? profiler shows a spike in kernel fallback events at t+300s during canary. can we see logs?

profiler-bot: log excerpt:
```
2026-03-16T12:03:21Z [runtime] kernel_select: prefer_opt=true, selected=fast-gemv-v2
2026-03-16T12:03:22Z [runtime] kernel_select: prefer_opt=false, fallback=scalar-loop (reason=small_batch, kv_prefetch_block)
2026-03-16T12:03:22Z [runtime] admission: sampled_reject id=abc123 token_est=120 target=80 p=0.3
```

sam: fallback to scalar-loop is red flag — it's happening when small batches + kv prefetch contention align. maybe our kernel hint heuristics need another threshold.

maya: proposal: add a minimum batch size hint to kernel_selector that overrides probabilistic admits for the first 25ms after a request arrives (grace period). also tie prefetch windows to admit probability: if p<0.5, reduce prefetch depth so we don't stall kernel pipeline on misses.

dan: sounds reasonable. let's also log kv-prefetch-latency per request so we can correlate with kernel fallback. keep canary running for another 30m and gather p90/p99.

lyra: one caution — reducing prefetch depth might lower kv_hit_rate and increase token costs. we should simulate offline with traffic replay.

maya: doing a replay now (small cluster). I'll post results when done. early numbers: kv_hit_rate down 3%, but p99 latency for evicted requests improved 18%.

ops-bot: canary health snapshot: 10% traffic, error_rate=0.12% (baseline 0.09%), avg_token_cost -3%, p99_lat_global -6%

sam: error bump looks acceptable if it's transient. Maya, when you have replay data paste the key graphs (kv hit vs p99 vs token_cost). we want solid numbers before wider rollout.

maya: ack. next steps: 1) replay with prefetch depth variants, 2) add pref_min_batch_ms=25ms grace to kernel_selector, 3) more telemetry for kv-prefetch-latency and kernel-fallback_reason. will update thread. :eyes:

lyra: also add a short experiment where admit sampling uses per-client smoothing (so bursty clients don't get hammered). could help fairness.

dan: good call. keep it lightweight. we don't want explosion of per-client state. a single EWMA on recent accepts should suffice.

maya: creating a follow-up PR and a metrics dashboard. thanks all :)
